html:
The Coyutecos were a Nahua people of the Pacific side of western Mexico, in the coast and hills of what is now western Jalisco, around Banderas Bay and the present Puerto Vallarta.

Their speech was a western form of Nahuatl. Spanish expeditions under Francisco Cortés de San Buenaventura reached this coast in 1524, and the region was soon divided among Spanish encomenderos. Little else is recorded of them; like many small peoples of the west coast they lost their language and merged into the mestizo population during the colonial period. Their neighbours to the north included the Cora.
sum: The Coyutecos were a Nahua people of the Pacific side of western Mexico, in the coast and hills of what is now western Jalisco, around Banderas Bay and the present Puerto Vallarta.
